subject: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sara.huang@acme.ai
Cc: ops@acme.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan

Morning team and Sara —

Quick retrospective from this week's sprint that clipped Acme's pilot throughput and left them throttled on 2 critical demo days. I attached q2_gpu_velocity.csv (exported token/sec by deal + hour) and the draft MOP we used with Acme (acme_mop_draft.pdf).

Top-level asks:
- Can infra confirm true available burst GPUs next week (how many, which zones)?
- Finance: are we comfortable approving the short-term burst uplift at list rate with a usage credit reconciliation afterwards?
- Sales/AE: can we tighten the immediate MOP language so Acme knows fallback behavior and expected latency during high concurrency?

Why this matters: Acme is on a tight pilot timeline — we under-provisioned because our velocity model didn't capture their daytime spike pattern (attached CSV shows a 3x spike Thu 14:00–16:00 PDT). If we don't fix now we risk the renewal conversation becoming reactive.

Proposed short-term plan (suggested):
1) Reserve 4 GPUs as a burst pool for Acme next Tue–Thu (local to us-west-2).
2) Finance provision a temporary usage credit for overage to avoid stalls; reconcile after pilot window.
3) Update the MOP to add an explicit fallback model variant (lower-cost quantized) and a 2-minute throttling policy.

I'm happy to run a 20-min triage today 3pm PT to lock decisions. Please reply with availability or ship answers inline.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0137

Attachments: q2_gpu_velocity.csv (csv), acme_mop_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sara.huang@acme.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan

Connor — thanks for the data and flagged impact. I pulled the infra telemetry and here's what I see: the w/peak on Thu collided with two other pilot customers in us-west-2 during the 14:00–16:30 window. We had limited burst slots that got consumed in-flight and the system fell back to queued requests.

Short answers inline: 
- Available burst GPUs next week: nominal pool for Tue–Thu is 6 gpus in us-west-2; after planned maintenance on Wed night we effectively have 4 immediately available without disrupting other reserved commitments.
- Zone constraints: these are all in the primary pool (us-west-2a/2b) — we can pin Acme to 2a for the burst pool to reduce interference.

Operational suggestion: provision 4 GPUs pinned to us-west-2a Tue–Thu and increase KV cache TTL for Acme to reduce repeated token recomputation during the spike window. That should cut perceived latency for the same cost tier.

I can join 3pm PT.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Operations
laura_bennett@redwood.com

> > Morning team and Sara —
> > 
> > Quick retrospective from this week's sprint that clipped Acme's pilot throughput and left them throttled on 2 critical demo days....

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sara.huang@acme.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan

Laura / all — good catch. From FinOps side: short-term burst is fine but we need a one-line commercial commitment: either (A) customer pays list rate for overage and we issue a usage credit if we determine the spike was our routing/caching fault, or (B) we provide a capped time-boxed credit (e.g., up to $3k) and opt-out to reconcile at pilot close. 

Operational knobs to minimize spend:
- Enforce the lower-cost quantized fallback for non-critical demo calls (Connor, can you confirm which demo flows MUST be high-precision?).
- Use KV cache TTL bump (Laura suggested) — that will save token compute, which is the bulk of the delta.

I side with the capped credit approach (B) for speed — preserves the pilot relationship and avoids a long approval chain. If leadership needs a larger cap we'll pull them in.

Ben Carter
Head of FinOps
ben_carter@redwood.com

> On 2027-08-23T10:05:00-07:00, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Connor — thanks for the data and flagged impact....

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, sara.huang@acme.ai
Date: 2027-08-23T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan

All — can confirm we can pull 4 GPUs from our internal burst slack for Tue–Thu and pin them to 2a. I'll prepare a short runbook (sprint-runbook.md) with the exact switch-over steps and health checks (success criteria, rollback path, contacts).

My proposed sequence: 
1) Tue 06:00 PT: Increase KV TTL for Acme to 300s (Laura).
2) Tue 08:00 PT: Deploy quantized fallback variant behind a feature flag for non-critical endpoints (Karthik).
3) Tue 09:00 PT: Provision & pin 4 GPUs to Acme; assign monitoring alerts to Marissa and Laura.
4) Wed/Thu: FinOps (Ben) monitors usage; reconcile after pilot window and apply capped credit if our routing caused the spike.

Sara — Connor, can you confirm which endpoints in the demo set are non-negotiable for full precision? If we can swap 30% of calls to the quantized variant during the spike it should make the pool last without further uplift.

Marissa Cole
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-23T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pipeline → GPU velocity retrospective and next-week capacity plan

Thanks everyone — clear path. Summarizing decisions and next actions (owners):

Decisions:
- We will provision a 4-GPU burst pool pinned to us-west-2a Tue–Thu next week. (Marissa / Laura to execute)
- FinOps approves a capped reconciliation credit of up to $3,000 for the pilot overage. (Ben)
- Deploy quantized fallback for non-critical demo endpoints and increase KV TTL for Acme to 300s. (Karthik / Laura)
- Sales will add explicit fallback language to the MOP; Connor to send updated paragraph by EOD Fri. (Connor)

Action items:
- Marissa: create sprint-runbook.md with switch-over steps and monitoring playbook. Due: Mon 08/30 EOD.
- Laura: schedule the pin & increase KV TTL on Tue 06:00 PT and confirm via the infra channel.
- Ben: approve the capped $3k credit and confirm accounting flow for reconciliation.
- Karthik: prepare quantized fallback behind feature flag and the small AB test to validate quality regression risk.
- Connor: update MOP paragraph and share to the Acme point-of-contact (Sara) and copy ops@acme.ai.

Connor — I'll follow up with a short calendar invite for Tue 05:50 PT to confirm readiness. If anyone objects to the $3k cap, flag now.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: sprint-runbook.md (will be added by Marissa), q2_gpu_velocity.csv, acme_mop_draft.pdf
